housing.summary: February 2026 indicative average asking rent for a 1-bedroom city-centre apartment: EUR 1,081.07 (https://finorum.com/rent-prices-europe-2026/). Finnish security deposits usually equal two months' rent and may not exceed three months (https://infofinland.fi/housing/rental-home/tenancy-agreement). Vuokraovi identifies itself as Finland's largest rental-home search marketplace (https://www.vuokraovi.com/).

banking.summary: Nordea's official newcomer page says applicants need a valid accepted identity document, proof of right of residence in Finland, and its completed customer form; a Finnish personal identity number is recommended and speeds the process. https://www.nordea.fi/en/personal/bank-with-us/become-a-customer/new-to-finland.html
required_docs: Valid passport or accepted EEA identity card
Residence permit, pending-application certificate, or EU right-of-residence registration

schools.summary: Helsinki offers fully English IB study, a fully English Finnish national upper-secondary track, and an American High School diploma option; the same City of Helsinki page lists Helsinki's international and language-programme schools. https://www.hel.fi/en/childhood-and-education/general-upper-secondary-education/studies-in-general-upper-secondary-school/general-upper-secondary-education-in-different-languages
curricula: Finnish national general upper secondary education in English

legal_admin.summary: Foreign newcomers should request a Finnish personal identity code and, if eligible, a municipality of residence online, then book and attend a Digital and Population Data Services Agency appointment in person within one month with the required identity and residence, work, or study evidence. https://dvv.fi/en/foreigner-registration
legal_admin.registration_step: Submit the DVV online foreigner-registration request, then attend an in-person DVV appointment within one month.

tax_finance.summary: A worker who needs a Finnish personal identity code for tax purposes must book and visit an issuing Tax Administration service point, complete form 6150e plus form 5057e (stay up to six months) or 5042e (stay over six months), and bring identity, work, and where applicable residence-right documents. https://www.vero.fi/en/individuals/tax-cards-and-tax-returns/arriving_in_finland/work_in_finland/finnish-personal-identity-codes-for-workers-arriving-in-finland/
tax_finance.tax_id_name: Finnish personal identity code (required to obtain a tax card or tax number)

transport.summary: Helsinki Region Transport (HSL) operates the capital-area network; most of Helsinki is in zones AB and an adult AB season ticket costs EUR 61.60 per 30 days with a yearly commitment. https://www.hel.fi/en/urban-environment-and-traffic/getting-around-helsinki-tips-for-newcomers Driving-licence exchange timing depends on the issuing country. https://traficom.fi/en/drivers-and-vehicles/driving-licenses/exchanging-foreign-driving-licence-finnish-driving-licence Registered Helsinki residents are automatically assigned a local health station by home address. https://www.hel.fi/en/health-and-social-services/welcome-helsinki-tips-for-health-and-social-services/welcome-helsinki-health-services
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licences remain valid until expiry; Contracting State licences must be exchanged within two years after permanent relocation; other recognised-country licences are valid for one year after population-register entry. Apply through Ajovarma. https://traficom.fi/en/drivers-and-vehicles/driving-licenses/exchanging-foreign-driving-licence-finnish-driving-licence
transport.healthcare_registration: Register as a Helsinki resident; the city then automatically assigns a health station based on the home address. The city also advises applying for a Kela card shortly after arrival. https://www.hel.fi/en/health-and-social-services/welcome-helsinki-tips-for-health-and-social-services/welcome-helsinki-health-services
